summary: Established an AIDE-based file integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04). Installed aide/aide-common, confirmed the distro's default config already covers /etc recursively via a catch-all '/ Full' rule (excluding /proc, /sys) plus curated per-package rules, and added an explicit '/etc Full' fragment for clarity. Built and installed the baseline database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db (70,163 entries) with creation timestamp and sha256 recorded under /var/lib/aide/baseline-meta/. Verified change detection by creating a test file under /etc, confirming aide --check flagged it as added, then removing it and confirming a clean state. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline state, issued a native reboot, polled until SSH returned, proved boot_id changed, and confirmed post-restart that the baseline database was byte-identical (same sha256), /etc still matched the baseline, and change detection still worked correctly.
actions_performed: Installed aide and aide-common via apt on node1
Inspected AIDE's default Debian/Ubuntu config and confirmed /etc is covered by a catch-all '/ Full' rule plus curated per-package rules
Added /etc/aide/aide.conf.d/50-etc-full-baseline.conf with an explicit '/etc Full' recursive rule
Ran aideinit to build the baseline database and promoted aide.db.new to the active aide.db
Recorded baseline metadata (creation timestamp and sha256 of aide.db) under /var/lib/aide/baseline-meta/
Verified detection by creating /etc/aide-baseline-test.conf, confirming aide --check flagged it as added, then removing it
Captured pre-restart boot_id and confirmed baseline health with zero /etc diffs
Issued a native reboot (shutdown -r now) on node1; acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until SSH access returned and confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart
Post-restart, verified aide.db sha256 was unchanged, /etc still showed zero diffs against baseline, and change detection still worked (new /etc file flagged, then cleaned up)

evidence.summary: AIDE installed, baseline database built covering /etc via root-level Full rule plus explicit /etc Full fragment; database installed as active aide.db with 70,163+ entries
Creation timestamp and sha256 checksum of aide.db recorded under /var/lib/aide/baseline-meta/

evidence.requirement: Baseline actually detects later changes to /etc
evidence.summary: Created /etc/aide-baseline-test.conf; aide --check reported it as added (f++++++++++++++++: /etc/aide-baseline-test.conf); test file removed afterward
Captured boot_id 35c87ec9-1707-4fb3-ab1d-f264d3618caa and confirmed aide.db sha256 4503abdf...bda2828 with zero /etc diffs before restart
Issued shutdown -r now on node1; command acknowledged and connection dropped as node went down

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Polled node1 (connection refused while down), then confirmed new boot_id 615f60f8-dfac-4439-b5d2-bc082ff1f3c6, different from pre-restart value

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of baseline and /etc integrity data
evidence.summary: Post-restart aide.db sha256 matched pre-restart value exactly, /etc showed zero diffs against baseline, and a newly created /etc test file was correctly flagged then cleaned up, proving the baseline and detection remained fully functional after restart
